title: Inventory Count Delivery Receipt Form
subtitle: Reconcile the promised inventory count delivery with actual units, condition, custody, evidence, exceptions, receiving decision, and accountable handoff.
description: An original, fillable inventory count delivery receipt form for controlling controlled physical inventory count and reconciliation package through delivery receipt identity, observations, evidence, decision, exceptions, escalation, completion, handoff, and final verification without replacing applicable requirements or professional review.
use_case: Use at Inventory control review and posting queue when inventory control or financial record owner and the delivering custodian need one receipt that separates physical handoff from inspection, hold, commercial acceptance, and exception resolution.

sections.title: Inventory Count condition inspection and receipt evidence
sections.guidance: Preserve observations made before the receiver changes packaging, custody, or physical condition.

blocks.label: Inventory Count receipt inspection
items: Count zone and physical boundaries match the assigned sheet
Location label, SKU, description, and unit of measure are unambiguous
Sealed cases, open packs, eaches, weight, or volume are converted consistently
Lot, serial, expiry, revision, ownership, and status are captured where required
Receiving, shipping, transfer, and work-in-process cutoff is respected
Damaged, quarantined, consigned, customer-owned, or obsolete stock is separated
First count is independent and corrections remain traceable
Recount uses the specified independence and evidence rule
Empty locations and unlisted stock are explicitly recorded
Unresolved identity, ownership, cutoff, or quantity issue is escalated before posting

blocks.label: Receipt evidence index
blocks.guidance: Record only necessary proof and preserve privacy or security restrictions.

blocks.label: Condition, count, custody, and acceptance narrative

fields.label: Condition, count, custody, and acceptance narrative

blocks.guidance: Describe facts that cannot be reconstructed from the line table or evidence reference.

sections.title: Inventory Count exception, containment, and escalation
sections.guidance: Make the trigger, affected scope, immediate control, owner, deadline, and escalation reconstructable.

blocks.label: Inventory Count exception indicators
items: Unlabeled, duplicate, or inaccessible location
Unknown item, lot, serial, owner, or inventory status
Mixed unit of measure or pack conversion is uncertain
Physical movement occurred outside the documented cutoff
First count and recount remain outside the threshold
System shows stock where location is empty or the reverse
Damaged, hold, consigned, or customer-owned quantity is commingled
Count sheet or scan batch is missing, altered, or duplicated
Scale, scanner, or system interface is unavailable
Potential fraud, diversion, or deliberate record override requires escalation
blocks.guidance: Select every observed condition; do not use a generic exception mark when the actual trigger is known.

sections.title: Inventory Count receipt decision and custody transfer
sections.guidance: Separate physical custody from final commercial, quality, safety, or financial acceptance.

blocks.label: Delivery and receiving attestation
blocks.guidance: Attestation confirms the recorded physical event, not waiver of a concealed issue or unresolved review.

sections.title: Inventory Count delivery receipt closeout and accountable handoff
sections.guidance: Close only when outcome, remaining limitation, next action, evidence, and receiving ownership agree.

blocks.label: Final outcome, handoff, and record location
Record boundary and stop condition
blocks.guidance: Use this inventory count delivery receipt with the applicable customer commitment, carrier terms, site policy, and retention requirements. Do not infer acceptance or release from a signature alone; unresolved identity, count, condition, custody, or proof issues require an owner, escalation, and documented disposition.
